basis.pressure: P(t) = P0*(1 - t/tau)**gamma, tau = m0/m_dot0 — isentropic rigid-tank blowdown; the solver's constant-T model differs by a bounded systematic bias (see sensitivity_case_a)

checks.basis: P(t) = P0*(1 - t/tau)**gamma, tau = m0/m_dot0 — isentropic rigid-tank blowdown; the solver's constant-T model differs by a bounded systematic bias (see sensitivity_case_a)

basis.throttle: (md_open - md_closed) / md_open — valve-step flow reduction (1 = fully shut, 0 = no effect)
basis.control_sync: max |t_event - round(t_event/dt1d)*dt1d| over valve events — millisecond control vs 1-D solver grid alignment

checks.basis: ms valve step must throttle the outlet by > 50%
valve events must sit on the 1-D grid within 0.1 ms
field variant must engage the reverse branch (rise > 0)

min_exchange.criterion: interface error <= tolerance (conservation) AND mean latency <= budget; periods below the 1-D step clamp to dt1d because a window shorter than one 1-D step carries no new information — the tight-coupling limit T_exch = dt1d is therefore the minimal feasible period

sensitivity.conclusion: The ~1.7% Case-A pressure deviation is a bounded, documented difference between the analytic baseline's isentropic power-law blowdown and the solver's constant-T rigid-tank model — NOT a numerical error (solver matches its own closed-form ODE to <0.01%) and NOT a reverse-coupling artifact (uncoupled 1-D reproduces the same value; 3-D feedback excursion is ~0.5 Pa). It grows monotonically with the horizon and is flat in nozzle parameters, as an accumulating model bias should.
